departing_trials.source_excerpt: abstract arm-level counts (percentage-corroborated): RESULTS: Diarrhea developed in 39 (29.3%) of 133 patients randomized to receive Lactobacillus GG and in 40 (29.9%) of 134 patients randomized to receive placebo (P=.93).

Can 2006 (PMID 15740542) abstract: 'S. boulardii also reduced the risk of antibiotic-associated diarrhoea ... [four of 119 (3.4%) vs. 22 of 127 (17.3%), relative risk: 0.2; 95% confidence interval: 0.07-0.5]'. ENDPOINT CORRECTION (override): the abstract extractor took the trial's ANY-diarrhoea figure (9/119 vs 29/127, RR 0.3) but our outcome is ANTIBIOTIC-ASSOCIATED diarrhoea, which the same abstract reports separately as 4/119 vs 22/127 (RR 0.2).

Beausoleil 2007 (PMID 18026577) abstract: 'antibiotic-associated diarrhea occurred in seven of 44 patients (15.9%) in the lactobacilli group and in 16 of 45 patients (35.6%) in the placebo group (OR 0.34, 95% CI 0.125 to 0.944)'. SCALE CORRECTION (override): the abstract extractor pooled the source ODDS RATIO 0.34 into this RR-family pool; the per-arm counts give the count-based RR directly, consistent with the other count-based trials.

direction_policy: Estimate-absence transitions take precedence: numeric to absent RESULT_REMOVED; absent to numeric RESULT_ADDED; both absent NO_DIRECTION even if candidate k changes. For two numerical results, AWAY_FROM_NULL takes priority if any of larger absolute effect (absolute log ratio or absolute MD), narrower comparable CI, more favourable point, or newly favourable CI applies. Mixed signals are disclosed. A newly favourable CI with no prior CI is a new claim, never a computed narrowing. Otherwise weakening is TOWARD_NULL; unchanged point with membership change is MEMBERSHIP_ONLY. All outcomes here favour lower values except ovulation, which favours higher odds; harm disappearance is flagged for presentation favourability, never treated as evidence of safety.
